player_trend_effects.Warriors: Role-critical official season profiles support a strong middle platform through Fisher-Harris and established spine production through Martin/Egan. No new causal trend is inferred beyond published statistics.
player_trend_effects.Dolphins: Katoa carries the larger verified kicking burden; Katoa/Nikorima together provide 33 published 2026 try assists, while Tabuai-Fidow supplies high running and tackle-break production. Restored Dolphins personnel therefore strengthens an already productive attack rather than representing isolated returns.

matchup_memory: Dolphins beat Warriors 26-24 in Round 17. This is retained as genuine contrary evidence but not treated as proof of current superiority.
evidence_family_independence: Market is not independent corroboration. Official team availability, official player statistics, season/venue results, prior head-to-head and weather are treated as distinct evidence families.
strongest_opposing_case: Dolphins have won seven straight, already beat the Warriors this season, are restoring Cobbo, Nikorima and Finefeuiaki together, and their role-critical profiles show substantial creation through Katoa/Nikorima plus running threat through Tabuai-Fidow.
falsification: The Warriors edge should reduce further or switch if game-day lists materially weaken Warriors middle/spine continuity, if the Dolphins restored combinations remain intact while Warriors returns are restricted, or if reliable market movement continues materially toward the Dolphins without offsetting independent evidence.

decision.reason: The Warriors retain the stronger structural baseline, but the Dolphins counter-case now meets the accumulated-failure action rule: seven straight wins, prior head-to-head success and restored combinations with verified role-critical production. Confidence is compressed toward market rather than allowing the opposing case to remain descriptive only.
